analysis.investment_thesis: Mastek was a textbook fast grower — 23% revenue CAGR over 9 years — but the story has materially weakened with FY26 growth slowing to just 7%, pushing the PEG ratio into overvalued territory on current momentum. At P/E 12.8x, the valuation looks cheap on the surface, but only if growth re-accelerates; without that catalyst, it's a stalwart at best.
key_strengths: PEG on long-run CAGR (32.5% earnings CAGR, 9Y) looks compelling at 0.39 — but only the past matters if momentum has stalled
Excellent FCF quality: INR 515 Cr FCF in FY26 (up from 376 Cr) with 5/5 positive OCF years — the business genuinely converts earnings to cash
Low debt (D/E 0.20), ROCE of 18% and steady reserves growth signal a financially sound franchise
key_risks: Growth deceleration is the #1 Lynch red flag: revenue grew just 7.1% YoY in FY26 (vs 13% in FY25 and 19% in FY24) — the story is clearly weakening
PEG on recent earnings growth (~7.4% YoY in FY26) is ~1.73 — overvalued by Lynch's core metric at current growth rates
Finance costs surged from INR 6 Cr (FY19) to INR 44 Cr (FY24), reflecting acquisitive leverage; debt jumped to INR 583 Cr in FY25 before partial paydown
red_flags: Revenue growth collapsed from ~19% (FY24) to ~13% (FY25) to 7% (FY26) — a consistent deceleration trend, not a one-year blip
EBITDA was INR 455 Cr in FY25 vs INR 491 Cr in FY23 — stagnant for 2 years before a FY26 recovery, suggesting the business hit a ceiling post-acquisition integration
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Mastek was a beautiful story from 2017–2022 — a mid-cap IT niche player levered to UK government digitization and Oracle Cloud adoption, doubling revenue in 3 years through both organic growth and smart acquisitions. That's exactly the kind of "what do they do and why will it keep working" story I love. But when I look at what's happened since FY23, the engine has clearly downshifted. Revenue grew just 7.1% in FY26, net profit grew 7.4%, and finance costs have ballooned from near-zero to INR 44 Cr peak — signs that acquisition-driven growth is fading and the organic engine hasn't yet picked up the slack. On recent numbers, the PEG is 1.73, which is solidly in "don't buy" territory by my rules.

The saving grace is valuation discipline and cash generation — P/E of 12.8x, EV/EBITDA under 10x, and INR 515 Cr of free cash flow in FY26 mean you're not paying full price for a broken story. If management can reignite growth back to 15%+ (plausible given AI/cloud tailwinds and UK public sector digitization pipelines), the stock could re-rate meaningfully. But I need to see the acceleration before I buy, not before it happens. This is a stock to watch closely, not own today.
